lines.text: An Israelite who slaughters an ox, lamb, or goat must bring it to the Tent of Meeting entrance.
The Israelites must bring their sacrifices from the open fields to the priest, who splatters the blood on the altar.
God says the Israelites must no longer offer their sacrifices to golden calves, and this is a permanent statute.
No Israelite or foreigner living among them may eat blood, which makes atonement on their doorposts.
Anyone who eats an animal found dead or mauled by wild beasts must wash and bathe, or bear iniquity.
